scores.rationale: Highest measured reach. FACT: I re-read results/c3gen/mmp_reach_S1.json: 101/250 single-cut hits, 109 for any edit, and 77/101 hits come from analogs ranked 0-4. Because the rules are mined, they cover the long tail of substituents that hand-written SMARTS miss. The assets fit the laptop: about 1.6 CPU-h fragmenting on 3 workers and a capped DuckDB self-join at 2 GB that will spill to disk but finish. The rule DB is under 100 MB, so it ships to Kaggle as a dataset. One leak-free rule DB built on the union of bench keys is enough for evaluation. Two runtime estimates are wrong. (1) Fingerprints for 3k products take 3k x 11-16.5 ms = 33-50 s per molecule, not 3-6 s (FACT: prep_data fp_and_mass timings measured in the biotx and fpga probes). Scoring needs a Morgan-only stage 1 (0.7 ms each) and the full fingerprint on only the top 300-400. (2) Tautomer keys cost 54-138 ms each, so computing them on the top 200 adds 11-28 s. Dedupe on plain InChIKey14 and leave tautomer keys to the merge, which needs at most about 8 keys per molecule. With those two fixes it runs in about 10 s per molecule, which is under 30 min on 4 Kaggle CPU cores. The probe took 495 s for 250 molecules, so phase 1 is buildable in about 2 days. The +0.01 to +0.03 LB estimate is the most optimistic of the five, because it assumes Class-3 molecules have one-edit neighbours as often as the S1 congener series do. Eligibility is clean: RDKit, COCONUT and train only. Support from enveda-180 adds synthetic bias but no licence risk.

Its Seeds-B idea is the most valuable new idea in the set: take mass-shifted database neighbours of target minus d and score them with the memory-mapped pool_fp @ zlog. It does not depend on spectral analogs, which hedges the DEC-009 finding of spurious analogs. Hand-written chemistry also covers edits that MMP grammar misses: ±H2, ±H2O, lactonisation, methylenedioxy formation and generic hydrolysis. Its two-stage fingerprint scoring is the only correct runtime plan among the five. Measured reach is lower than MMP (29% on S3 against 42%), and the 45 SMARTS will miss the mined tail. One feasibility problem: the 4 h pool tautomer-key build is wasted CPU on a shared machine. Checking `forbidden` only needs the plain InChIKey14 and the skeleton key of the forbidden truths, which take seconds. Shift localisation needs train spectra mapped from InChIKey14 to spectrum rows, and that also works on Kaggle. Two-step formula-delta matching admits many chance matches (56-64% chance 2-step formula matches), so the n_steps penalty is essential. Eligibility is the cleanest of the five: own SMARTS, CC0/PD databases and own nets, with BioTransformer and MINE rules explicitly excluded. The +0.005 to +0.015 estimate is realistic.

FACT (ssr_probe_ceiling.txt): 32%/29% of truths are one substituent swap from a same-scaffold analog. Reach on rings>=3 falls to 0.43/0.29, so it is a subset of what MMP reaches rather than a different set. It needs the most bespoke code of the three edit-based designs: sugar-aware Murcko cutting, symmetry-unique site enumeration, a new fragment enumerator that keeps atom sets, and four edit families E0-E3. Its runtime budget assumes tautomer keys at 20 ms, but the measured cost is 54-138 ms, so its 13 s per molecule is really about 25-45 s unless tautomer keys are dropped. Its own LB arithmetic (+0.003 to +0.01, inside the noise) is honest. Two parts are worth taking: the per-atom shifted/unshifted site score s_a, and treating glycosides as substituents. Its pass/fail rule is good discipline: recall@200 < 0.08 on C3NP means drop the angle and move effort to same-formula ranking.

It has the lowest reach of the five by its own estimate (2-4% recall@200 on real Class 3), because it only makes formula-preserving moves. Its probe adds two useful facts. The window keeps the truth formula 96.8%/74% of the time, with the formula top-3 by population at 93%/67%. And the top-5 zlog same-formula isomers share the generic scaffold 56%/40% of the time, so the window is a better parent pool than the analogs. Feasibility is fine: the T1/T2 tables are 5-30 min on 3 workers and runtime is about 15 s with a hard cap. Moves M3/M4 (acyl migration, interglycosidic linkage) are fiddly to write as SMARTS. The eligibility score is lower because it correctly flags LIPID MAPS rows in the engine pool as having unverified licence terms. Those rows must be excluded from T1/T2 and from seeds until the terms are checked. This applies to every design that seeds from the engine pool or window, and fpga's 'CC BY 4.0' claim for LIPID MAPS is unverified. Better used as a move family inside mmp-edit (its same-mass 'move' edits) than built as its own generator.

It has the most assets: BRICS library, MMP table, atom-environment whitelist and a PubChem NP-prior sample, about 2-2.5 h of builds. It also has the most code: 5 operator families plus a GA loop. That is the hardest to finish and debug in about 5 days next to the bench builder and FPNet jobs. Optimising toward a linear zlog objective invites bit-stuffing. BRICS-style generation has already been flat in the competition (FACT intel: 0.046 -> 0.050; derivative enumeration 0.337 -> 0.335). Reach beyond 1-2 edits from analogs adds mostly decoys, because generated near-twins hurt ranking more than they help recall. Its measurements are useful: full fingerprint 16.5 ms, Morgan r2+r3 0.7 ms, Morgan-only Spearman 0.77 against the full score, tautomer key 138 ms. Three parts are worth keeping: Morgan-surrogate then full re-score, the analog-propagation score term A (sum of spectral_sim x Tanimoto), and the cheap evaluation trick of computing tautomer keys only for outputs with Tanimoto >= 0.5 to the truth. Its GA itself is not worth building now. Eligibility is fine if the GB-GA operators are reimplemented from the paper.

judge:2.best_ideas_to_graft:
Winner: mmp-edit (phase 1), extended with parts from the others. Ranked by value for the cost:
1. From biotx and fpga: two-stage scoring is mandatory. Score with the Morgan-only zlog slice first (0.7 ms each, Spearman 0.77 against the full score), and compute the full 6930-bit prep_data fingerprint on only the top 300-400. mmp-edit's own estimate of 3-6 s for 3k fingerprints is really 33-50 s.
2. From fpga and biotx: never compute tautomer keys inside generate (54-138 ms each, FACT). Dedupe on plain InChIKey14 and let the merge compute tautomer keys only for the ≤8 generator slots actually used. Check forbidden through the plain InChIKey14 and skeleton keys of the forbidden truths. This removes biotx's 4 h pool tautomer-key build.
3. From biotx: Seeds B. For each of about 40 common deltas, take the zlog top-3 pool/COCONUT structures at target minus delta (from memory-mapped pool_fp/coco_fp) and use them as extra mmp-edit seeds. They do not depend on spectral analogs.
4. From formula-first: add the zlog top-5 same-formula window structures as parents for same-mass move edits. The probe shows they share the generic scaffold 56%/40% of the time, more often than the analogs do.
5. From biotx: about 10-15 atom-level SMIRKS as a third edit family, covering what MMP grammar misses: ±H2 (C=C, C=O/CHOH), ±H2O, lactonisation, catechol-OMe to methylenedioxy, prenyl+ortho-OH to dimethylchromene, and generic ester/glycoside hydrolysis.
6. From scaffold-decorate and biotx: run ModiFinder-style shifted/unshifted peak localisation (per-atom s_a) on only the top 100-300 products. It is the only signal that separates regioisomers, so gate it on a measured hit@25 gain. Also cut glycosides as substituents (sugar-aware cuts).
7. From fpga: the analog-propagation score term, sum of spectral_sim x Tanimoto(child, seed), and the CLI trick of computing truth-match tautomer keys only for outputs with Tanimoto >= 0.5.
8. From formula-first: exclude LIPID MAPS rows from every seed and prior table until their licence is verified.
9. From scaffold-decorate and fpga: decision discipline. Gate on C3NP recall@200 >= 0.08 and hit@25 >= 0.03, fit λ on a scaffold-split half, and never tune on S3, which looks leaky or easy for the ho1 nets.

Overall judgement on feasibility: mmp-edit with grafts 1-3 is buildable in about 2-3 days and runs at about 10 s per molecule, which is under 30 min for 400 molecules on 4 Kaggle cores and fits beside E6. Every design estimates +0.003 to +0.03 on the LB because the generated candidates sit below the engine and E6 entries. None of them closes the 0.072 gap alone. Generation is worth one focused build. Same-formula isomer ranking, the approach Udam disclosed at 0.414, should get equal effort.

scores.rationale: It has the best measured ceiling (FACT: 40/42% single-cut reach and 44/49% with 2-cut on S1/S3, 77/101 hits at analog ranks 0-4). Its rules are mined, so they cover the transforms the hand-written designs list plus the long tail. But its +0.01-0.03 LB claim is too high. (1) The reach was measured on Class-1/2 truths that have congeneric library series; Udam's ~3x deletion overstatement points to about 15-20% on real Class 3. (2) A placement factor of 0.4-0.7 is unrealistic when candidates start at slot >=4 or alternate with E6; 0.2-0.35 is more likely. (3) The positional-isomer ranking problem is not solved: the fragment-explanation term is 'phase 2' and unproven. My estimate: +0.004 to +0.012. Build risk: rdMMPA with H-cuts on 711k NPs (glycosides with 30+ cut sites) may run well above 8 ms/mol, so time 5k first. The const-group self-join is the memory hazard; the 64-member cap handles it. The leak control (asset C) is correctly specified and is mandatory. Eligibility is clean (RDKit, COCONUT, train, own nets). The one bias is enveda-180 synthetic rules, which support_coco weighting mitigates.

Its measured reach is lower than MMP's (FACT: 46%/29%, and only 17% one-step on S3), and the hand-written rule set is mostly a subset of what MMP mines. Its unique value: (a) Seeds B, mass-shifted database precursors ranked by zlog, a channel that does not depend on the spectral analogs DEC-009 found spurious in 38% of PubChem-only cases; (b) non-MMP chemistry (+-H2, +-H2O, lactonisation, catechol-OMe to methylenedioxy, prenyl to chromene) that MMP single cuts miss; (c) a generic hydrolysis rule; (d) the explicit drop of window/DB keys, which suits Class 3 exactly. The 4 h tautomer-key build for the pool is waste: the ik14 check against forbidden plus the existing pool_key.npy is enough for input filtering. Its +0.005-0.015 estimate is honest. The kill criteria (C3NP recall@200 <8%, merged gain <+0.01) are good. Eligibility is the cleanest of the five: all-own SMARTS, and BioTransformer/MINE rules are explicitly not used.

Its own probe shows it is dominated by MMP: 32/29% reach for 'same scaffold + <=1 swap' against MMP's 40/42%, with the same edit families. Its self-estimate of +0.003-0.01 sits inside the noise floor, and its arithmetic (3-way round robin, ~3.5x dilution) is the most honest of the five. It is worth keeping for parts, not as a standalone build: (1) the sugar-aware Murcko core, which cuts glycosides off as substituents; (2) the cleanest ModiFinder site-evidence formula (per-atom log ratio of shifted vs unshifted fragment intensity, plus a template-support threshold so wrong-core noise ranks low); (3) the P(sub | env, scaffold class) prior with the forbidden-key exclusion; (4) E3 cross-recombination of decorations between templates that share a core. The MADGEN oracle-scaffold anchor (10.5% top-1) usefully calibrates what scaffold-given generation can do.

It restricts itself to formula-preserving moves, so its reach is the lowest: its own estimate is 9-14% on S1, 4-6% on S3, and 2-4% on real Class 3, for +0.002-0.006. The S3 ranking figure (81% top-1) it flags itself as suspect. Its key insight is a FACT worth grafting: the zlog-best same-formula window structures share the truth's generic scaffold (56% of top-5 on S1) 2-4x more often than spectral analogs carry the truth formula. So the top window entries by fpscore should be first-class parents for every generator, not only for same-mass moves. The formula prior (truth formula top-3 in 93%/67% from population alone) is useful as a cheap filter on two-step mass decompositions. The M3/M4 moves (acyl and glycosyl migration on sugars) cover a real NP isomer class that MMP covers poorly. Eligibility: it correctly flags LIPID MAPS rows in the engine pool as unverified. Exclude them from any table.

It has the widest search space in principle, but the bottleneck everyone measured is ranking among near-isomers, and the GA makes that worse. Thousands of archive members, optimised against zlog itself, are adversarial decoys: bit-stuffing and zlog-hacking against a linear objective with 4743-bit Morgan surrogate Spearman 0.77. Its build (5 assets, ~2.5 h) and tuning surface (~10 knobs, 5 operator weights) are the heaviest of the five, against the scarcest validation data (250-300 molecules). Step 3, the one-shot mass repair, is just the MMP/biotx generator, and G1 already admits the fallback. Its valuable measured facts and engineering pieces: the full 6930-bit fp costs 16.5 ms and the tautomer key 138 ms per molecule, so a Morgan-only stage-1 prefilter is required; evaluation should compute tautomer keys only for outputs with ECFP Tc >=0.5 to the truth; the analog-propagation term A (spectral_sim x Tc to seed) is the strongest single channel in the intel. The optional zlog-margin promotion is also worth keeping. Eligibility is fine if GB-GA is re-implemented; it is slightly riskier for its reliance on a PubChem-sample NP prior and unverified operator code provenance.

judge:1.best_ideas_to_graft:
VERDICT (INFERENCE): build ONE generator, with mmp-edit as the backbone and biotx as a small second rule family inside it. Do not build five. None of the designs closes the 0.072 gap. Realistic merged gain is +0.005 to +0.015, and the two levers below could perhaps double that. The common bottleneck is the same in every design: ranking positional and substituent isomers. Reach is not the bottleneck.

Grafts into mmpedit, in priority order:
1. Drop any product whose key is in the +-5 ppm PubChem/COCONUT window (from biotx and ffiso). FACT from the host: a Class-3 truth is in neither PubChem nor COCONUT. The window is already in ctx, so the lookup is free. It removes real-DB decoys and duplicates of E6 and the engine. mmpedit currently omits it.
2. Window parents (from ffiso). FACT: the zlog-best same-formula window structures share the truth's generic scaffold in 56% of S1 cases (top-5). Seeds should be the top-20 analogs, plus the top ~10 window entries by fpscore, plus biotx Seeds B (database structures at target-minus-delta, ranked by zlog). Seeds B do not depend on spectral analogs, which DEC-009 found spurious in 38% of PubChem-only cases.
3. A non-MMP edit family (from biotx): about 10-15 hand SMARTS for +-H2, +-H2O, lactonisation, prenyl to chromene, catechol-OMe to methylenedioxy, generic ester/glycoside hydrolysis, and ffiso M3/M4 acyl and glycosyl migration on sugars.
4. Sugar-aware fragmentation (from SSR): cut glycosidic units off first, so hexose and deoxyhexose swaps are single edits even on large glycosides.
5. Site localisation (SSR's per-atom log ratio of shifted vs unshifted fragment intensity, plus a template-support threshold). This is the only proposed signal against the isomer bottleneck. Make it phase 1, not phase 2: measure hit@25 with and without it on C3NP npex before any other tuning.
6. Runtime and evaluation tricks (from fpga). FACT: the full fp costs 16.5 ms and the tautomer key 138 ms per molecule. Use a Morgan-only stage-1 prefilter to the top ~400, then the full fp. Never compute tautomer keys inside generate (plain ik14 dedupe; the merge already dedupes on the metric key). In the CLI, compute the truth-match key only for outputs with ECFP Tc >= 0.5.
7. zlog-margin promotion (from fpga and Ahmed's gate idea): if the best generated product's full zlog exceeds the best window or engine zlog by a margin, give the generator slot 2 or 3. Otherwise start appending at slot >= 4. FACT: SV library-hit lists must stay >= 0.92. Tune the margin so the gate almost never fires on SV and S1. This is where most of any real LB gain would come from, because with append-at-slot-4 a perfect generator hit is worth at most 1/4.
8. Priors: the SSR P(sub | env, scaffold class) and the biotx rule-path prior. Weight support by COCONUT over train (enveda-180 is synthetic). Exclude every bench, C3NP and held_S4 key at build time.

Evaluation discipline. FACT: C3NP already exists, with subsets npex 250, s3pc 215 and s3none 85, plus forbidden.parquet (671 keys). Use s3none and npex as the primary judges; s3none is the most Class-3-like. Run a single 10-minute reach oracle on C3NP before building assets: union of the MMP 1-cut, biotx rule and window-parent reach. Use a scaffold or mid split for the lambda fit. Never tune on S3/s3pc, which shows suspicious zlog easiness (84% top-1). Kill rule: merged C3NP gain < +0.01 or any SV drop > 0.002. Skip biotx's 4 h pool tautomer-key build, the fpga GA loop, and LIPID MAPS rows in any prior table.

scores.rationale: Best-grounded design. Its reach probe (FACT: 40%/42% single-cut, 44%/49% any edit on S1/S3) uses the same truth-removal logic as C3NP, and C3NP is these same 550 molecules (npex 250, s3pc 215, s3none 85; I checked). Data-mined rules carry support priors and cover the dominant edits (CH3, hexose, OH, OMe), with leak control (asset C) built in. The cost estimates are wrong, though. Scoring 3k products takes 3k x 11-16.5 ms = 33-50 s, not 3-6 s, using the timings the biotx/fpga probes measured. Tautomer keys on the top 200 take 11-28 s (54-138 ms each, measured). It needs the Morgan-only prefilter and plain-ik14 dedupe. On ranking, positional variants of 20 seeds are near-twins, and zlog's measured in-window MRR is 0.47 against about 60 real decoys, so expect much worse against 600+ siblings. The +0.01-0.03 LB claim is optimistic: E6 realised half its proxy (+0.005 vs +0.010). A realistic figure is +0.005-0.015. Eligibility is clean: RDKit, COCONUT and train, nothing NC. Leak risk stays low only if asset C excludes truths by both ik14 and ckey (stereo/tautomer twins) and the eval DB is never reused for tuning.

Its seed B is the most valuable novel idea: mass-shifted DB neighbours (target minus a rule delta) ranked by zlog. It does not depend on spectral analogs, which are spurious for 38% of the PubChem-only bucket (DEC-009). It also covers non-MMP edits (±H2, epoxide, lactonisation, methylenedioxy, hydrolysis) and the removal direction. Reach is lower than MMP on S3 (29% vs 42%), because a fixed rule list misses lipid homologation and the rare acyl and sugar variants. About 45 hand-written SMARTS plus removal graph code is a lot of labour and a source of chemistry bugs. Leak risks: (1) the rule priors are mined from train/COCONUT pairs with no stated truth exclusion, so the truth-to-analog pair inflates its own rule's prior on the bench; (2) seed B needs a forbidden check by tautomer key over 772k pool structures, a 4 h build, and a skipped or partial build lets the truth enter as a seed (delta-0 rules, hydration/dehydration round trips). Ranking: 2-step products face thousands of siblings, so the 2-step hit@25 is probably near zero. Stage-1 Morgan scoring is correctly specified. Eligibility is clean: own SMARTS, BioTransformer/MINE rule files explicitly excluded.

Mostly a subset of mmp-edit's reach. Same scaffold within one swap: 32%/29%, against MMP's 40%/42%. It adds sugar-aware coring and cross-template recombination (E3), and the latter has unmeasured value. Runtime is under-costed: fingerprints at 1 ms (measured 11-16.5 ms) and tautomer keys at 20 ms (measured 54-138 ms) put the real figure at 40-60 s per molecule without a surrogate prefilter. A new atom-set fragment enumerator plus per-atom site scores is substantial new code, and the localisation signal is unproven. Leak hygiene is good: A1 is built with the forbidden union excluded. The weights are fitted on half of C3NP and reported on the other half, but n=275 per half makes the grid noisy. Its own estimate (+0.003-0.01, inside LB noise) and the honest kill rule are credible. Eligibility is clean.

Narrow reach: formula-preserving moves only, about 9-14% simulated on S1 and 4-6% on S3. Its measured finding is valuable, though. Truth-removed same-formula window isomers ranked by zlog carry a same-generic-scaffold relative in the top 5 for 56%/40% of molecules, 2-4x more often than spectral analogs (FACT). That makes the zlog-ranked window a better seed source for every generator. It also measured zlog's discrimination among real same-formula isomers (S1 top-1 28.9%, MRR 0.465), the best calibration available for the 'would our nets rank it' question. It correctly flags S3 as suspiciously easy (0.878 MRR). Eligibility risk: the engine pool includes LIPID MAPS rows whose licence is unverified. Exclude them from T1/T2 and from window seeds unless confirmed. The T2 leak rule is stated. Fingerprint cost at 3 ms is under-estimated (11-16.5 ms). Positional moves on glycosides explode.

The most complex design: a GA plus 5 assets (BRICS, MMP, an environment whitelist, an NP prior drawn from a PubChem sample, SMARTS), about 2.5 h of builds, and the most tuning knobs. Optimising a linear bit-weight zlog is a recipe for adversarial 'zlog hacking'. The GA finds bit-stuffed molecules that outscore the truth, which directly hurts the 'truth ranked high among decoys' criterion; the A3 gate only partly mitigates this. Leak risk: A2 (MMP), A3 (environment whitelist) and A4 have no stated exclusion of bench truths. A2 counts of 3 or more reduce single-pair leakage but do not remove it. Eligibility risks: GB-GA operator code licence (reimplementation required), and a LIPID MAPS CC BY assumption that has not been verified. Its own probe timings (full fingerprint 16.5 ms, Morgan-only 0.7 ms, tautomer key 138 ms, Morgan-only MRR 0.36 vs 0.47) are the most useful measured engineering facts across all five designs. Its analog-propagation fitness term is a good idea. As a standalone generator it is the lowest priority.

judge:3.best_ideas_to_graft:
WINNER: mmp-edit as the backbone, with biotx as its second edit family. Graft the following into it:
1. **Seed union** (the biggest graft):
   - spectral analogs (mmp);
   - the top 5-10 zlog-ranked same-formula window structures (formula-first FACT: a same-generic-scaffold relative 2-4x more often than analogs);
   - biotx seed B: pool and COCONUT structures at target minus each of the ~40 rule deltas, ranked by zlog, top 3 per delta. This is independent of the spurious-analog problem (38% in DEC-009).
2. **Three edit families under one mass-first planner** (biotx step 4: keep only rule multisets within 10 ppm):
   - mined MMP rules with support priors;
   - about 10-15 biotx SMIRKS for non-MMP chemistry (±H2, epoxide, lactonisation, methylenedioxy, generic hydrolysis);
   - formula-first M1/M2/M4 positional moves for Δ≈0, which applies to 19-26% of molecules (same-formula analog present).
3. **Mandatory two-stage scoring and runtime discipline** from fpga/biotx measurements:
   - Morgan-only partial zlog (0.7-1 ms) prefilters to about 400, then the full 6930-bit fingerprint (11-16.5 ms).
   - No tautomer keys inside generate beyond the final ~25 (54-138 ms each); dedupe on plain ik14 and let the merge dedupe on the metric key.
   - The mmp, SSR and ffiso runtime estimates are 5-10x low without this.
4. **fpga's analog-propagation term**, Σ spectral_sim × Tanimoto(child, seed), plus rule support with COCONUT support weighted up, as priors next to z(fp·zlog).
5. **Site localisation as one shared module.** Use the SSR/ModiFinder shifted-vs-unshifted peak logic, but validate it cheaply before relying on it. Test: take train library pairs that are one edit apart and both have spectra, and measure whether the scorer picks the right site. Then consider ICEBERG/GLACIER (MIT, MassSpecGym) re-scoring of the top 50 within the same formula, the only proven positional discriminator (v4n uses it).
6. **Leak hygiene across every mined asset** (MMP rules, biotx rule priors, SSR A1, ffiso T1/T2, fpga A2/A3):
   - Exclude the C3NP forbidden union plus held_S4 by both ik14 and ckey (stereo/tautomer twins).
   - Keep separate eval and submission builds.
   - Add a leak canary: run once with a truth-including DB and once with the excluded one; a large gap means memorisation.
   - The forbidden check on seed B needs pool tautomer keys, or at least ik14+ckey via results/c3np/work/canon_cache.pkl.
7. **Evaluation discipline:**
   - Report C3NP per subset (npex / s3pc / s3none). The s3none subset (85, closest to true Class 3) is the honest headline. Never tune on S3/s3pc, since zlog is suspiciously easy there (0.84-0.88 top-1).
   - Tune λ on npex even mids only.
   - Use the biotx/fpga kill gates: recall@200 < 8%, or a merged C3NP gain < +0.01.
   - Discount all LB projections by about 2x: E6 realised +0.005 against a +0.010 proxy.
8. **Eligibility:** exclude LIPID MAPS rows from all seeds and assets until its licence is verified (formula-first flagged this; fpga assumed CC BY). Reimplement any GB-GA or BRICS operators; copy no code.
